labels.label: N4:M1
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. GX.PunctDisc.cls_boundary is a real relation in mathlib's FundamentalGroup of the subspace punctDisc a = [-1,1]x[0,a] minus the points (0, j+1/2). It is not a quotient that trivialises, and the punctures really are removed (the field ∀ j < a, z ≠ (0, j+1/2)). boundary is the counterclockwise rectangle boundary from (-1,0). lasso k = tL · sq · tL⁻¹ goes round the square [-1,1]x[a-k-1, a-k], which contains puncture a k. I checked the telescoping by hand for a = 2: concatenating the lower lasso and then the upper one gives the boundary, so the mathlib product [γ₀]*…*[γ_{a-1}] is the concatenation γ_{a-1}⋯γ₀ (FundamentalGroup is End at this pin, and mul_def is xs * ys = ys ≫ xs, which confirms the kb proposal). cls_lasso_eq_small and discP_small do give a small positive loop: smallSq is the explicit counterclockwise square with corners (±r, c±r) around the puncture, for every 0 < r < 1/2. dist_smallSq_le puts it within sup-distance r. discP_small fits it into any neighbourhood U of ext(p_k) whenever the closed-disc parametrisation ext is continuous at p_k, and that hypothesis is satisfiable and natural. discHol_eq_prod pushes the relation through any continuous φ, and theoremM applies it to every homomorphism ρ, which is Lean ≥ notes. Disclosed and not formalized: freeness of π₁ (not needed for the statement), the G̃ total-angle sentence, and the product/cyclic-order convention (a fair question; the closer's ordering claim checks out, see minor finding 1 for the arc wording). The REPORT calls 'D₋ a disc' carried, but embeddedness is dropped, so 'weakened' would be the exact word. That direction is harmless.

labels.label: N4:M3
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. InteractionData.holIn_eq_holOut is a direct use of mk_eq_conj_of_annulus. That lemma is a correct and non-trivial statement (Φ : I×I → X with Φ(s,0) = Φ(s,1) = τ(s) gives [Φ(0,·)] = [τ·Φ(1,·)·τ⁻¹]), proved by pulling the null-homotopy of the square's boundary through Φ. No field of InteractionData contains the conclusion (#print checked). annulus_one fixes only the orientation in which the outer circle runs, and the docstring and SCOPE (c) disclose that this makes the future parametrisation orientation-reversing for Σ. FINDING CHECKED, TRUE. NOTES l.329 defines P(x) with one notion of 'positive'. BBS l.621-623, which N4 itself cites for the orientation, orients every HS-surface by the SO₀(1,2)-invariant orientation of HS². With every loop Σ-positive and C± = ∂D±, the annulus joins C₋ to C₊⁻¹, so hol(C₋)hol(C₊) = 1. That is N3's ∏P_i = 1 (l.214-216, 227-229) and N5's 'P_in⁻¹ by Theorem M' (l.477). Then (M3) holds iff hol(C₋)² = 1 (SphereData.holIn_mul_holOut and holIn_eq_holOut_iff, both correct). Under the other reading (outgoing loops transported, Σ-negative), N4 holds but N5 l.477 would read P_in, not P_in⁻¹. So the notes mix conventions whichever reading is taken, and 'one convention has to be fixed' is the right framing. The counterexample m3_printed_fails is a legitimate, non-degenerate witness. It takes M = ℂ∖{0} (the regular part of a sphere with one incoming and one outgoing particle, a = b = 1). C₋ is the counterclockwise unit circle (cWinding +1 around 0). C₊ is the clockwise circle of radius 2, which is the positive boundary of {|z| ≥ 2} ∪ {∞}: cWinding +1 around w = 0 in the holomorphic chart w = 1/z. The annulus is (1+s)e^{2πit}, and the hypothesis g² ≠ 1 is satisfiable (probe: G = Multiplicative ℤ, g = ofAdd 1). Because the theorem holds for every group, including abelian ones, it also refutes the 'up to conjugacy' reading. The Lean witness is topological: ρ_g = g^wind is not shown to be an HS holonomy (SCOPE (f), [r]). It refutes 'at the level of holonomy, this is topology' (l.345). For the geometric statement I checked the [r] argument independently, and it is right. The link of a point on a massive particle line is a causally regular type-1 HS-sphere with a = b = 1, the Σ-positive loops at its two cone points are inverse in π₁ = ℤ, and the holonomy is an elliptic rotation R with R² = 1 iff the cone angle is π. The corrected form (transported orientation) is proved as stated. The Σ-positive reformulation hol(C₋) = P(q_b)⁻¹⋯P(q₁)⁻¹, with the q labelled in Σ-positive order, is not a separate theorem but follows in one line from sphere_relation. The real-angle half Θ₋ = Θ₊ is not stated, and that is disclosed with a true obstruction: there is no HS² (G,X)-model, no ℝP¹-circle and no G̃ in gx, lean-causal or mathlib at this pin (grep: GX.Suspension.* is generic, with no HS² instance).

labels.label: N4:theorem-M
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. GX.theoremM gives (M1), (M2), (M3) and conservation for every ρ : π₁(M,x₀) →* G, and the fourth conjunct is the composite of the first three. theoremM_developing and theoremM_singular do instantiate. ρ is obtained from GX.developing_theorem_fundamentalGroup together with a dev satisfying IsGXMorphism and equivariance, so it is the holonomy of a developing pair, not a free parameter. theoremM_singular takes M = reg S = (Sing G X S)ᶜ with GX.regChartedSpace and hasGroupoid_regChartedSpace. Both add standing hypotheses of gx's developing theorem; see minor finding 2. Since theoremM holds for every ρ, the two corollaries add instantiation, not mathematics, and the docstring says as much. SphereData.sphere_relation is derived from the annulus alone, without a full sphere decomposition, which is Lean ≥ N3. The physical reading (masses, Θ < 2π, (M4)) is not formalized, as disclosed.

findings.what: 'Every system of disjoint arcs from a boundary point to the punctures is such an image [of the model's tethers]' is false as written. The model's tethers are not disjoint: tL k is an initial segment of tL (k+1), all of them run up x = -1, smallTether k = tL k · dBL, and adjacent squares sq k share a horizontal edge. The image of overlapping paths overlaps, so no disjoint arc system is literally their image. The true statement, and the one the relations use, holds up to homotopy rel endpoints. After a homeomorphism of the closed disc taking the punctures to the model's, every disjoint arc system in the cyclic order is homotopic, in the punctured disc, to the model's tethers perturbed apart. The lasso classes depend only on the tethers' homotopy classes, so nothing proved is affected.
findings.fix: Write 'is, after a homeomorphism of the disc and up to homotopy rel endpoints in the punctured disc, such an image (Schoenflies; classical, not formalized)' in SCOPE (a) and in the REPORT note. Optionally say that the model's tethers overlap along x = -1 and are separated by an arbitrarily small perturbation in the order stated in SCOPE (c).
